subproblem.title: Continuity of the inverse of a proper injective chart (Simon Ch. 2, (4.1)–(4.2))
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^d, W ⊆ ℝ^P and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P. Assume ψ is continuous on V and injective on V, ψ(V) ⊆ W, and V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W. Then for every v ∈ V and ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ satisfies |v' − v| < ε. Distances are Euclidean. No openness of V or W is assumed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P), ContinuousOn ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V ⊆ W → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → ∀ v ∈ V, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ v' ∈ V, dist (ψ v') (ψ v) < δ → dist v' v < ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2, §4, Definition (4.1) and the remark before (4.2) (book/chapter-02.txt, lines 849–862). There Simon notes that "the above definition ensures the local representation is a homeomorphism of V onto the image M ∩ W"; the properness condition of (4.1) is what makes this work. This child is step 2 of the parent proof (node chart_tangent_space), restricted to the hypotheses that step actually uses. Openness of V and W is not needed. Distances are Euclidean.
Fix v ∈ V and ε > 0, and write q := ψ(v).
1. Suppose, for a contradiction, that no δ > 0 has the stated property. Then for every j ∈ ℕ the number δ = 1/(j+1) > 0 fails. So there is v_j ∈ V with |ψ(v_j) − q| < 1/(j+1) and |v_j − v| ≥ ε.
2. We have 0 ≤ |ψ(v_j) − q| < 1/(j+1) and 1/(j+1) → 0. By squeezing, ψ(v_j) → q as j → ∞.
3. Let K := {q} ∪ {ψ(v_j) : j ∈ ℕ}. K is compact because it is the range of a convergent sequence together with its limit. Indeed, given an open cover of K, one member contains q, and by step 2 it contains ψ(v_j) for all j ≥ j₀. Finitely many further members cover ψ(v_0), …, ψ(v_{j₀−1}).
4. K ⊆ W. For each j, v_j ∈ V, so ψ(v_j) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ W. Also v ∈ V, so q = ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ W.
5. By the properness hypothesis applied to the compact set K ⊆ W, the set C := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact. Every v_j lies in C, because v_j ∈ V and ψ(v_j) ∈ K. C is a compact subset of the metric space ℝ^d, hence sequentially compact. So there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a point v* ∈ C with v_{φ(i)} → v* as i → ∞. In particular v* ∈ V.
6. Now v* ∈ V, every v_{φ(i)} lies in V, and v_{φ(i)} → v*. Since ψ is continuous on V, it is continuous at v* relative to V, so ψ(v_{φ(i)}) → ψ(v*). On the other hand, (ψ(v_{φ(i)}))_i is a subsequence of (ψ(v_j))_j, so ψ(v_{φ(i)}) → q by step 2. Limits in ℝ^P are unique, hence ψ(v*) = q = ψ(v).
7. Both v* and v lie in V, and ψ is injective on V, so v* = v. Thus v_{φ(i)} → v. Hence |v_{φ(i)} − v| < ε for some i. This contradicts step 1, which gives |v_j − v| ≥ ε for every j, in particular for j = φ(i).
8. So the assumption in step 1 is false. There is δ > 0 such that every v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ satisfies |v' − v| < ε. Since v ∈ V and ε > 0 were arbitrary, the statement is proved.
proof_key_steps: Negating the claim gives v_j ∈ V with |ψ(v_j) − ψ(v)| < 1/(j+1) and |v_j − v| ≥ ε, so ψ(v_j) → ψ(v).
K = {ψ(v)} ∪ {ψ(v_j)} is compact and lies in W, so V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact and contains every v_j.
A subsequence v_{φ(i)} converges to some v* ∈ V. Continuity of ψ on V and uniqueness of limits give ψ(v*) = ψ(v).
Injectivity on V gives v* = v, which contradicts |v_{φ(i)} − v| ≥ ε.

audit.reason: The prose and standalone Lean proposition agree, including the absence of openness assumptions. The proof constructs a convergent image sequence whose range plus limit is compact and contained in W. Properness supplies a subsequence limit inside V; relative continuity and injectivity identify it with v, contradicting the fixed positive separation. Every step is justified without invoking the child or parent conclusion.

subproblem.title: Every vector Dψ(v)a is the velocity of a C¹ curve in N
subproblem.statement: Let P, r, d ∈ ℕ with r ≥ 1, N ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^d open, and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P of class C^r on V with ψ(V) ⊆ N. Then for every v ∈ V, Dψ(v)(ℝ^d) ⊆ tangentSpace N (ψ(v)), where Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v. Here tangentSpace N y is the set of w ∈ ℝ^P for which some γ : ℝ → ℝ^P is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps (−1, 1) into N, and satisfies γ(0) = y and γ'(0) = w (HasDerivAt γ w 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P r d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P), 1 ≤ r → IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V → ψ '' V ⊆ N → ∀ v ∈ V, Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v) ⊆ tangentSpace N (ψ v)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2, §4, the definition of T_yM and (4.3) (book/chapter-02.txt, lines 865–871), which says the vectors D_jψ(x) lie in T_yM. This child is step 6 of the parent proof (node chart_tangent_space). All norms are Euclidean.
0. Fix v ∈ V and put A := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v. Since r ≥ 1, ψ is C¹ on V. V is open and v ∈ V, so ψ is C¹ on a neighbourhood of v. Hence ψ is Fréchet differentiable at v, and its derivative there is fderiv ℝ ψ v = A. Let w ∈ A(ℝ^d), say w = Aa with a ∈ ℝ^d. We must produce γ : ℝ → ℝ^P that is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps (−1, 1) into N, and has γ(0) = ψ(v) and γ'(0) = w.
1. Case a = 0 (parent step 6(a)). Then w = A0 = 0. Take the constant curve γ(t) := ψ(v). It is C^∞, so C¹ on (−1, 1). It maps (−1, 1) to {ψ(v)} ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N. Also γ(0) = ψ(v) and γ'(0) = 0 = w.
2. Case a ≠ 0 (parent step 6(b)). V is open and v ∈ V, so choose ρ₀ > 0 with ball(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V. (The parent uses closedBall(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V. Either works, since only points at distance ≤ ρ₀/2 < ρ₀ from v are used.) Put c := ρ₀/|a| > 0 and h(t) := t/(1 + t²/c²) for t ∈ ℝ.
 (a) The denominator satisfies 1 + t²/c² ≥ 1 > 0. So h is a quotient of C^∞ functions with nonvanishing denominator, hence C^∞ (in particular C¹) on ℝ. Also h(0) = 0.
 (b) By the quotient rule, h'(t) = ((1 + t²/c²) − t·(2t/c²))/(1 + t²/c²)² = (1 − t²/c²)/(1 + t²/c²)². So h'(0) = 1.
 (c) |h(t)| ≤ c/2 for every t ∈ ℝ. Indeed |h(t)| = |t|/(1 + t²/c²) = c²|t|/(c² + t²). Also c² + t² − 2c|t| = (c − |t|)² ≥ 0, which gives c²|t| ≤ (c/2)(c² + t²).
3. Let β(t) := v + h(t)a for t ∈ ℝ. By 2(c), |β(t) − v| = |h(t)||a| ≤ (c/2)|a| = ρ₀/2 < ρ₀. So β(t) ∈ ball(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V for every t ∈ ℝ. By 2(a), β is C¹ on ℝ and β(0) = v + 0·a = v. By 2(b), β has derivative h'(0)a = a at t = 0.
4. Let γ := ψ ∘ β, that is, γ(t) = ψ(v + h(t)a) (parent step 6(c)). For t ∈ (−1, 1), β(t) ∈ V, so γ(t) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ N. Also γ(0) = ψ(β(0)) = ψ(v).
5. γ is C¹ on (−1, 1) (parent step 6(d)). β is C¹ on (−1, 1) and maps it into V, and ψ is C¹ on V. So the composition ψ ∘ β is C¹ on (−1, 1).
6. Chain rule (parent step 6(e)). ψ is differentiable at β(0) = v with derivative A, and β has derivative a at 0. So γ = ψ ∘ β has derivative A(a) = w at 0.
7. Hence γ witnesses w ∈ tangentSpace N (ψ(v)). Since w ∈ A(ℝ^d) was arbitrary, Dψ(v)(ℝ^d) ⊆ tangentSpace N (ψ(v)).
proof_key_steps: From r ≥ 1 and V open, ψ is C¹ on V and differentiable at v with derivative A = fderiv ℝ ψ v.
For a = 0, the constant curve ψ(v) has velocity 0 = A0.
For a ≠ 0, let c = ρ₀/|a| and h(t) = t/(1 + t²/c²). Then h is smooth, h(0) = 0, h'(0) = 1 and |h| ≤ c/2, so β(t) = v + h(t)a stays in ball(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V.
γ = ψ ∘ β is C¹ on (−1, 1) and maps into ψ(V) ⊆ N. Also γ(0) = ψ(v), and γ'(0) = Aa by the chain rule.

audit.reason: The statement and Lean type agree. Openness and r ≥ 1 justify the ambient derivative. The constant curve handles a = 0; otherwise the explicitly smooth rational reparametrization has derivative 1 at zero and keeps the parameter curve strictly inside V. Composition gives a C¹ curve on the entire required interval, and the chain rule gives velocity Dψ(v)a. The construction is complete and independent.

subproblem.title: Secant estimate at a chart point from differentiability, an injective derivative and inverse continuity
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, N ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^d, W ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P, A : ℝ^d → ℝ^P a continuous linear map, and v ∈ V. Assume ψ(V) = W ∩ N, ψ is Fréchet differentiable at v with derivative A, and A is injective. Assume also the inverse-continuity condition at v: for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ satisfies |v' − v| < ε. Then for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every y ∈ N with |y − ψ(v)| < δ admits some a ∈ ℝ^d with |y − ψ(v) − Aa| ≤ ε|y − ψ(v)|.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (A : Euclid d →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (v : Euclid d), IsOpen W → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → v ∈ V → HasFDerivAt ψ A v → Injective A → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ v' ∈ V, dist (ψ v') (ψ v) < δ → dist v' v < ε) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ N, dist y (ψ v) < δ → ∃ a : Euclid d, ‖y - ψ v - A a‖ ≤ ε * ‖y - ψ v‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2, §4 (book/chapter-02.txt, lines 849–871). This child is steps 1, 3 and 4 of the parent proof (node chart_tangent_space). Step 4(a) of the parent uses the inverse continuity (ii); here that property is a hypothesis.
Write q := ψ(v). All norms are Euclidean.
1. Lower bound for A (parent step 1). If d = 0, then ℝ^d = {0}. Put m := 1; then |Aa| ≥ m|a| holds because a = 0. If d ≥ 1, the unit sphere S = {a ∈ ℝ^d : |a| = 1} is nonempty and compact. The function a ↦ |Aa| is continuous on S. It is positive on S, because A is injective and a ≠ 0 gives Aa ≠ 0. Hence m := min_{a∈S} |Aa| exists and m > 0. For a ≠ 0, linearity gives |Aa| = |a|·|A(a/|a|)| ≥ m|a|, and a = 0 is trivial. In both cases m > 0 and |Aa| ≥ m|a| for all a ∈ ℝ^d. (Equivalently, an injective linear map on a finite-dimensional space is antilipschitz.)
2. Differentiability estimate (parent step 3). ψ has Fréchet derivative A at v, so ψ(v') − q − A(v' − v) = o(|v' − v|) as v' → v. Hence for every η > 0 there is ρ(η) > 0 such that |ψ(v') − q − A(v' − v)| ≤ η|v' − v| for all v' ∈ ℝ^d with |v' − v| < ρ(η).
3. Apply step 2 with η = m/2 and let |v' − v| < ρ(m/2). Step 1 and the triangle inequality give m|v' − v| ≤ |A(v' − v)| ≤ |ψ(v') − q| + |ψ(v') − q − A(v' − v)| ≤ |ψ(v') − q| + (m/2)|v' − v|. Therefore (m/2)|v' − v| ≤ |ψ(v') − q|.
4. Choice of constants (parent step 4). Let ε > 0. Put η := min(m/2, εm/2) > 0 and ρ := min(ρ(η), ρ(m/2)) > 0.
 (a) Apply the inverse-continuity hypothesis to ρ > 0. This gives δ₁ > 0 such that every v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − q| < δ₁ satisfies |v' − v| < ρ.
 (b) q = ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ N, so q ∈ W. Since W is open, there is δ₂ > 0 with ball(q, δ₂) ⊆ W. Put δ := min(δ₁, δ₂) > 0.
5. Let y ∈ N with |y − q| < δ. Then |y − q| < δ₂, so y ∈ W, and hence y ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V). So y = ψ(v') for some v' ∈ V. Since |ψ(v') − q| = |y − q| < δ₁, step 4(a) gives |v' − v| < ρ. In particular |v' − v| < ρ(η) and |v' − v| < ρ(m/2).
6. Put a := v' − v. Step 2 with η gives |y − q − Aa| = |ψ(v') − q − A(v' − v)| ≤ η|v' − v|. We have η ≤ εm/2, and step 3 gives (m/2)|v' − v| ≤ |y − q|. Therefore |y − q − Aa| ≤ (εm/2)|v' − v| = ε·((m/2)|v' − v|) ≤ ε|y − q|.
7. So δ > 0 has the required property for this ε. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, the statement is proved.
proof_key_steps: Injectivity of A on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^d gives m > 0 with |Aa| ≥ m|a|.
Differentiability at v gives ρ(η) with |ψ(v') − ψ(v) − A(v' − v)| ≤ η|v' − v| whenever |v' − v| < ρ(η). With η = m/2 this yields (m/2)|v' − v| ≤ |ψ(v') − ψ(v)|.
Set η = min(m/2, εm/2) and ρ = min(ρ(η), ρ(m/2)). Take δ = min(δ₁, δ₂), where δ₁ comes from inverse continuity at ρ and ball(ψ(v), δ₂) ⊆ W.
Each y ∈ N with |y − ψ(v)| < δ equals ψ(v') with v' ∈ V and |v' − v| < ρ. Then a := v' − v gives |y − ψ(v) − Aa| ≤ ε|y − ψ(v)|.

audit.reason: The type matches the hypotheses: W is open, v belongs to V, A is the injective derivative at v, and inverse continuity is explicit. The lower bound handles d = 0 separately. The differentiability estimates, positive radius choices, image equality and choice a = v' − v yield precisely the stated relative-error bound. No openness of V or unstated sibling theorem is used.

subproblem.title: Under a secant estimate, curve velocities lie in the range of A
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, N ⊆ ℝ^P, q ∈ ℝ^P, and A : ℝ^d → ℝ^P a continuous linear map. Assume that for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every y ∈ N with |y − q| < δ admits some a ∈ ℝ^d with |y − q − Aa| ≤ ε|y − q|. Then tangentSpace N q ⊆ A(ℝ^d). Here tangentSpace N q is the set of w ∈ ℝ^P for which some γ : ℝ → ℝ^P is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps (−1, 1) into N, and satisfies γ(0) = q and γ'(0) = w (HasDerivAt γ w 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (q : Euclid P) (A : Euclid d →L[ℝ] Euclid P), (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ N, dist y q < δ → ∃ a : Euclid d, ‖y - q - A a‖ ≤ ε * ‖y - q‖) → tangentSpace N q ⊆ Set.range A
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2, §4, the definition of T_yM and (4.3) (book/chapter-02.txt, lines 865–871). This child is step 5 of the parent proof (node chart_tangent_space). The secant estimate, conclusion (iii) of the parent, is the hypothesis here. All norms are Euclidean.
1. L := A(ℝ^d) = Set.range A is a linear subspace of ℝ^P, being the image of a linear map. Its dimension is at most d, so it is finite-dimensional and therefore closed in ℝ^P. It contains 0, so it is nonempty. For u ∈ ℝ^P let dist(u, L) := inf_{ℓ ∈ L} |u − ℓ|. Then dist(u, L) ≥ 0, and dist(u, L) ≤ |u − ℓ| for every ℓ ∈ L. The map u ↦ dist(u, L) is continuous (indeed 1-Lipschitz). Since L is closed and nonempty, dist(u, L) = 0 implies u ∈ L.
2. Let w ∈ tangentSpace N q, witnessed by γ : ℝ → ℝ^P. So γ maps (−1, 1) into N, γ(0) = q and γ has derivative w at 0. The C¹ property of γ is not needed. Differentiability of γ at 0 means the difference quotients s(t) := t⁻¹(γ(t) − γ(0)) = t⁻¹(γ(t) − q), for t ≠ 0, satisfy s(t) → w as t → 0 with t ≠ 0. It also implies that γ is continuous at 0.
3. Fix ε > 0 and let δ > 0 be given by the hypothesis for this ε. γ is continuous at 0 and γ(0) = q, so there is t₁ > 0 with |γ(t) − q| < δ whenever |t| < t₁. Put t₀ := min(t₁, 1) > 0.
4. Let 0 < |t| < t₀. Then t ∈ (−1, 1), so γ(t) ∈ N, and |γ(t) − q| < δ. The hypothesis gives a_t ∈ ℝ^d with |γ(t) − q − Aa_t| ≤ ε|γ(t) − q|. Also A(t⁻¹a_t) = t⁻¹Aa_t ∈ L. By step 1, dist(s(t), L) ≤ |s(t) − A(t⁻¹a_t)| = |t⁻¹(γ(t) − q − Aa_t)| = |t|⁻¹|γ(t) − q − Aa_t| ≤ ε|t|⁻¹|γ(t) − q| = ε|s(t)|.
5. Let t → 0 with t ≠ 0; this punctured-neighbourhood filter on ℝ is nontrivial. By step 2 and the continuity of dist(·, L) and of the norm, dist(s(t), L) → dist(w, L) and ε|s(t)| → ε|w|. The inequality of step 4 holds whenever 0 < |t| < t₀, that is, eventually along this filter. Passing to the limit gives dist(w, L) ≤ ε|w|.
6. Step 5 holds for every ε > 0. Given e > 0, take ε := e/(|w| + 1) > 0. Then dist(w, L) ≤ e|w|/(|w| + 1) ≤ e. Since e > 0 is arbitrary, dist(w, L) ≤ 0. Together with dist(w, L) ≥ 0, this gives dist(w, L) = 0.
7. By step 1 (L is closed and nonempty), w ∈ L = A(ℝ^d). Since w ∈ tangentSpace N q was arbitrary, tangentSpace N q ⊆ A(ℝ^d).
proof_key_steps: L = A(ℝ^d) is a finite-dimensional, hence closed, nonempty subspace, and dist(·, L) is continuous.
For w = γ'(0) and 0 < |t| < t₀, the secant estimate gives dist((γ(t) − q)/t, L) ≤ ε|(γ(t) − q)/t|.
Letting t → 0 gives dist(w, L) ≤ ε|w| for every ε > 0, so dist(w, L) = 0.
Since L is closed, w ∈ L = A(ℝ^d).

audit.reason: The prose matches the exact curve-based tangentSpace contract. The proof establishes that the range is closed and nonempty, bounds its distance from each small difference quotient, and passes to the derivative along the nontrivial punctured real neighbourhood filter. Choosing ε = e/(‖w‖ + 1) correctly includes w = 0. Neither q ∈ N nor injectivity of A is an additional requirement.
